records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.panel` has both `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)` doing the same job of pushing the panel right; order(3) is a no-op today while margin does the work, and the two redundant mechanisms will silently conflict if future order values are added.
records.rationale: The diff shows `.panel` is being pushed right by `margin-left: auto;`, while `@include order(3);` only sets flex item ordering (see `@mixin order($val) { ... order: $val; }`) and does not “push the panel right.” Thus the finding’s claim that both mechanisms “do the same job of pushing the panel right” is a misread of what `order` does in flexbox.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] header.scss 36-37: `.panel { @include order(3); }` with no `order()` on other children makes header layout depend on implicit/explicit ordering spread across two stylesheets; any new child (e.g., plugin outlet element) defaults to order 0 and slots before the title
records.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed into a flex container (`@include flexbox();`) and `.panel` is given `@include order(3);` plus `margin-left: auto;` while other sibling elements (e.g., the former `.title` block) no longer have explicit positioning/order in this diff. With only one child having an explicit flex `order`, any additional sibling inserted into `.contents` will default to `order: 0` and be laid out before the `.panel`, which can make the header layout more brittle as new children are introduced.
